notes: Summary: Steadfast is a Tier-1 telco platform looking to offload conversational and ranking workloads from in-house endpoints. Strong emphasis on predictable spend and hard latency SLOs for customer-facing flows.
Primary workloads: customer_support_chat (multi-turn), personalization_ranking (real-time 10s-100s QPS per shard), semantic_search for agent assist, embeddings for offline indexing.
Target SLOs: 50ms p50, 95ms p95 for single-turn routing on small-chat model; 120ms p95 for multi-turn with KV cache. For ranking endpoints target 30ms p95 at 200 QPS sustained.
Throughput constraints: baseline sustained QPS ~2k (global), with burst capacity to 10k for promotions. Want autoscale but backed by reserved capacity to guarantee throughput under load.
Preferred models: open-weights Llama-3 variants and a tuned reranker; will accept quantized variants. Wants ability to pin model versions and fall back to a cheaper quantized variant automatically.
Deployment constraints: VPC-first, need option for on-prem air-gapped install in specific regions for regulated customers. KMS integration mandatory; audit logs retained 1 year.
Security asks: SSO via SAML, SOC2 coverage, contractual data residency (NA only for first phase). Asking about HSM support for key wrapping (raised by security team).
POC ask (proposed): 6-week pilot on Dedicated with 4xA10-equivalent GPUs reserved per region (NA-east + NA-west), canary traffic routing, telemetry hook into their APM.
Base cost model we provided (internal):
- Assumptions: 4 reserved GPUs region A + 4 reserved GPUs region B = 8 GPUs total.
- Vendor price: $3.50/GPU-hour (example Redwood committed price for quoted hardware) -> monthly cost = 8 * 24 * 30 * 3.5 = $20,160
- Operational add-ons (support, observability retention): flat $6k/mo
- Total committed cost/mo = $26,160
Utilization & unit economics (conservative):
- Effective token throughput per GPU-hour (with batching + KV cache): 120M tokens/hour at 8-bit quantized LLM (workload-mix weighted).
- If they utilize 50% of committed capacity (conservative for early months) -> 60M tokens/hour effective -> monthly total tokens = 60M * 24 * 30 = 43.2B tokens
- Amortized infra cost per 1M tokens = $26,160 / 43,200 = ~$0.606 per 1M tokens (note: this excludes downstream network/storage costs and SRE time).
- If utilization increases to 80% (target steady state) -> cost per 1M tokens falls to ~$0.38 per 1M tokens.
- Additional costs: model licensing (if any), egress, optional private control plane fee (one-time/recurring), and incident response retainer.

Batching and KV cache effects: assuming average request length 60 tokens and average generated tokens 40, with prefix KV cache hit-rate 35% for multi-turn -> reduces per-request compute by ~25% in practice; included in 120M tokens/hr figure.

Routing/fallback policy: propose primary on Dedicated, fallback to Redwood Hosted API cheaper quantized variant when utilization > 90% or during maintenance windows. Need to confirm acceptable latency delta on fallback.

SLA negotiation points raised by customer: uptime floor (99.9% vs 99.95%), credits calculation (pro rata vs layered), maintenance window advance notice (30 days vs 7 days), scheduled kernel/driver updates exclusion from SLA or not.
Procurement questions outstanding: holdback terms, indemnity on training data exposure, export controls for on-prem package, acceptance tests for POC (p95 latency, throughput, error-rate targets).

Quoted commercial path: 6-month pilot (discounted commitment), then 12–24 month committed capacity contract with tiered pricing by commit level. Pricing sensitivity: finance wants to see 20–30% unit cost decline at 12-month steady state to justify buy-in.

Sales tactics: recommend showing 3 commit scenarios (conservative 4 GPUs, mid 8 GPUs, aggressive 16 GPUs) with utilization bands (40/60/80%) and per-1M-token economics; include a sample fallback costing spreadsheet.
Internal ask: SE to produce a modeling spreadsheet with sensitivity to cache hit-rate, tokens per request, batching factor, reserved GPU price +/-10%, and optional dedicated network egress fee.

Customer quote snippets: 'We need predictable dollars per contact agent handled' — product lead. 'If your committed model doesn't show 30% savings vs our current infra at scale we won't move' — infra head.

Risks: procurement timeline (legal/finance) could push close beyond Q1; air-gap/on-prem asks could add significant integration time and cost; fallback latency delta may break tight SLO customer flows.
Decision criteria: clear unit economics at 60–80% utilization, SLAs that reflect real maintenance cadence, and a working KMS + VPC peering runbook.

Recommended next steps (operational): 1) Diego to deliver sensitivity model (by 2024-12-08). 2) Pricing team to provide 3 commit-tier SOWs. 3) Security to sign KMS/HSM design doc and sample contract language. 4) Agree on POC acceptance criteria and schedule start date.
Contact rhythm: weekly technical sync (Wed 10am PT), procurement checkpoint every other Friday. Point-of-contact: CTO (N. Patel) and Head of Infra (L. Romero).
